jobs.title: AI Research Resident (Algorithms Codesign)
jobs.jd:
NORMAL COMPUTING | BUILD WITH US

Normal is an applied AI company solving the hardest problems in AI and silicon. We build foundational hardware and software for the semiconductor industry, critical AI infrastructure, and the broader systems that power our world, in partnership with the world's most advanced institutions. We work as one team across New York City, Silicon Valley (Mountain View), and London.


THE RESIDENCY PROGRAM

The AI Research Residency is Normal Computing's flagship program for exceptional researchers and engineers who want to work at the frontier of AI. Residents join a small, hand-picked cohort with a dedicated research mentor, direct access to the team developing the algorithms for our in-memory inference hardware, and a clear arc from onboarding through publication.

Every residency is built around two milestones that mark you as part of something bigger than a single project: a research paper co-authored with our team, and a company-wide research colloquium where you present your findings to the full Normal Computing organization. You'll leave with a body of published, presented work, and a standing as one of the earliest residents to help define what this program becomes.


THIS TRACK: ALGORITHMS CODESIGN

Normal's hardware runs the most memory-bound parts of large-model inference inside memory itself, rather than shuttling weights to a processor. The software that makes this programmable doesn't exist yet in any standard form. This track is about the computational methods that make LLM inference run efficiently on it: rethinking how operations like attention, memory access, and long-context decoding should behave on hardware that computes inside memory, rather than adapting standard GPU kernels to a new chip.

You'll work on this as a co-design problem. The hardware and the algorithms are developed in parallel, so your findings feed architectural decisions rather than implementing against a fixed specification. You'll validate ideas against our simulators and FPGA prototypes first, and against silicon as it arrives.


YOUR NORMAL EXPERIENCE

This is a hands-on research residency: you'll take ownership of a real technical problem in inference algorithms for in-memory compute, work alongside the researchers and engineers building our platform, and be expected to contribute ideas, not just execute someone else's. Your job is to help turn research into production-quality research code that a team can build on. Outside-of-the-box thinking is encouraged.

You'll get direct exposure to the pace, ambiguity, and speed of decision-making that comes with working at a fast-moving, well-funded startup, where the distance between an idea on a whiteboard and a result on real hardware is measured in weeks, not years.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

Develop inference algorithms for in-memory hardware. Understand which parts of LLM workloads are best suited to in-memory execution and develop algorithms that exploit it natively, demonstrated first in simulation and then on hardware.

Design numerical methods that fit the physics. Design methods that exploit thermal noise and analog dynamics rather than working around them.

Build evaluation suites and benchmarks. Help build the evaluation frameworks and benchmarks that characterize how algorithms behave on real hardware and in simulation, and tell us honestly whether any of it actually works.

Translate workloads into hardware constraints. Turn insights about model workloads into constraints and opportunities for the hardware and architecture teams.

Prototype and iterate rapidly. Move with the hardware as it evolves from simulation to FPGA to silicon.

Drive a research question of your own. Partner with researchers and engineers to scope, run, and iterate on an original technical investigation, with rigorous experimental analysis and documentation along the way.

Co-author a paper. Work with the team to write up your findings for submission to a relevant venue, with mentorship on framing, experiments, and technical writing. One of the two milestones every resident builds toward.

Present at the residency colloquium. Share your work and thinking with the broader Normal Computing research community at the program's capstone event, and get real-time feedback from people building this technology every day.


WHAT WOULD MAKE YOU A GREAT FIT

Currently pursuing or recently completed a graduate degree (MS or PhD, or equivalent research experience) in machine learning, applied mathematics, physics, electrical engineering, computer science, or a related field. Publications are a strong plus, but not required at the resident level; a solid research track record is what matters.

A working understanding of large model inference: attention mechanisms, KV cache, long-context decoding, memory bandwidth constraints. Deep production experience isn't expected at the resident level, but the intuition should feel familiar.

Some exposure to inference optimization (quantization, sparsity, kernel fusion, or memory-efficient attention), or to stochastic systems, probabilistic methods, numerical analysis, or analog computation.

Strong Python skills, plus some experience with a systems language (C++, Rust, or similar) or with implementing algorithms close to hardware, beyond high-level frameworks.

Some experience (course projects, research, or otherwise) turning a research idea into working, reasonably reproducible code. You care about whether results replicate, not just whether a demo works once.

Comfort reasoning from first principles about what a novel substrate can do efficiently.

Bonus: exposure to analog or mixed-signal systems, in-memory compute, or non-von-Neumann architectures; publications or open-source work in efficient inference, stochastic algorithms, or novel computing; or experience working on hardware that did not yet exist when you joined.

Strong written and verbal communication skills; prior experience writing up research (papers, theses, technical reports) is a plus, as is any experience presenting technical work to a live audience.

A bias toward ownership and self-direction. You're energized, not overwhelmed, by the ambiguity and speed of a small, fast-moving startup.

jobs.title: Market Analyst - Power Trading Analytics
jobs.jd: Wood Mackenzie is the global leader in analytics, insights and proprietary data across the entire energy and natural resources landscape. For over 50 years our work has guided the decisions of the world’s most influential energy producers, utilities companies, financial institutions and governments. Now, with the world’s energy system more complex and interconnected than ever before, sector-specific views are no longer enough. That’s why we’ve redefined what’s possible with Intelligence Connected. By fusing our unparalleled proprietary data with the sharpest analytical minds, all supercharged by Synoptic AI, we deliver a clear, interconnected view of the entire value chain. Our trusted team of 2,700 experts across 30 countries breaks siloes and connects industries, markets and regions across the globe. This empowers our customers to identify risk sooner, spot opportunities faster and recalibrate strategy with confidence – whether planning days, weeks, months or decades ahead. Wood Mackenzie Intelligence Connected WoodMac.com Wood Mackenzie Brand Video Wood Mackenzie Values Inclusive – we succeed together Trusting – we choose to trust each other Customer committed – we put customers at the heart of our decisions Future Focused – we accelerate change Curious – we turn knowledge into action The Role We are seeking a full-time Power Market Analyst to join Wood Mackenzie’s Power & Renewables team, focusing on the development and application of advanced power market models across European electricity markets. As a Power Market Analyst, you will play a key role in building, maintaining, and enhancing market optimization models used to analyse power systems, generation economics, transmission constraints, and market outcomes. You will apply linear programming (LP) and other optimization techniques to simulate market behaviour, assess investment and operational decisions, and provide actionable insights on power market dynamics, decarbonization pathways, and energy transition challenges. Key Responsibilities Develop, maintain, and enhance optimization-based power market models for European electricity markets. Design and implement LP and mixed-integer optimization models to simulate generation dispatch, storage operation, cross-border trading, and market-clearing mechanisms. Analyse power market fundamentals, including supply-demand dynamics, renewable integration, fuel markets, emissions costs, and transmission constraints. Conduct scenario analysis to evaluate market outcomes, asset profitability, policy impacts, and energy transition pathways. Translate complex model outputs into clear market insights and recommendations for internal stakeholders and clients. Improve model methodologies, assumptions, and analytical frameworks to enhance model accuracy, transparency, and performance. Work with large datasets and develop efficient data workflows to support model development and analysis. Collaborate with experts across power markets, renewable energy, economics, and policy to deliver high-quality research and market intelligence. Monitor developments in European energy markets, regulatory frameworks, and market design, assessing their impact on market participants and investment decisions. Support client engagements through presentations, bespoke analyses, technical discussions, and thought leadership. About You We are looking for a highly analytical and intellectually curious individual with a strong foundation in optimization, quantitative modelling, and power market analysis. You enjoy solving complex problems, building robust models, and generating insights that support strategic decision-making. Essential Skills and Qualifications A degree in Operations Research, Engineering, Applied Mathematics, Economics, Energy Systems, Computer Science, or a related quantitative discipline. Experience in electricity market analysis, power system modeling, or energy economics. Strong knowledge of optimization techniques, particularly linear programming (LP) and mixed-integer programming (MIP). Experience developing and implementing mathematical models for power systems, generation portfolios, storage assets, or electricity markets. Proficiency in Python and/or other programming languages used for optimization and quantitative analysis. Experience with optimization frameworks and solvers such as Gurobi, CPLEX, Xpress, Pyomo, or similar tools. Strong understanding of European power market fundamentals, market design, and price formation mechanisms. Ability to analyze complex datasets and communicate technical findings clearly to both technical and commercial audiences. Strong problem-solving skills, attention to detail, and ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously. Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English. Why Join Us? At Wood Mackenzie, you will work on industry-leading power market models that help clients navigate rapidly changing energy markets and the transition to a low-carbon economy. You will collaborate with leading analysts, modelers, and industry experts to solve complex challenges facing power systems, renewable integration, energy storage, and electricity market design. This role offers an opportunity to apply cutting-edge optimization techniques and market analysis to inform investment decisions, support policy evaluation, and shape the future of the energy sector. Equal Opportunities We are an equal opportunities employer. This means we are committed to recruiting the best people regardless of their race, colour, religion, age, sex (including pregnancy, sexual orientation, and gender identity) , national origin, disability or protected veteran status. jobs.jd: COO | Regional Data Office | Associate, Data Management & Analytics Professional | New York About ING : In the Americas, ING’s Wholesale Banking division offers a broad range of innovative financial products and services to domestic and international corporate and institutional clients. When you come to work at ING, you’re joining a team where individuality isn’t just accepted, it’s encouraged. We’ve built a culture that’s fun, friendly and supportive – it’s the kind of place where you can be yourself and make the most of whatever you have to offer. We give people the freedom to take risks, think differently, take ownership of their work, and make great things happen. We’re here to help you get ahead. And with our global network, there’s plenty of scope to take your career in new directions, perhaps even ones you’ve never considered. ING Americas follows a hybrid work model, allowing for in-office / work from home flexibility. Hybrid work arrangements vary based on business area. Sound like the kind of place you’d feel at home? We’d love to hear from you. About the position: Data is at the heart of everything we do at ING. It powers how we measure risk, assess performance, and make decisions. To ensure we unlock the full value of our data, we must guarantee its completeness, accuracy, auditability, traceability, and protection. With emerging trends such as digital wallets on the horizon and increasing regulatory expectations around data governance, CDO is evolving to meet these challenges head-on, ensuring our data remains both a strategic asset and a safeguarded resource. ING Americas is looking for a Data Management and Analytics Professional who can connect data governance with practical delivery. In this role, you will help ensure that data deliveries, reporting solutions, and analytics capabilities are compliant by design, while identifying opportunities to simplify processes, strengthen controls, and automate recurring activities. You will work at the intersection of business, data, technology, risk, and regulatory requirements. Your contribution will help ING Americas deliver trusted data outcomes, improve operational efficiency, and strengthen audit and regulatory readiness. About the department: As COO Wholesale Banking Americas, we ensure our Wholesale Banking clients a superior customer experience with our scalable operations providing seamless, digital services, while staying safe & secure. COO department focuses on Client Service Delivery (CSD), Financial Crime Prevention (FCP), Operational Design Control and Resilience (ODCR), and the Regional Data Office (RDO). You will join the Regional Data Office Americas, part of COO Wholesale Banking Americas. The Regional Data Office drives the local execution of ING’s data strategy and supports the implementation of data governance, data quality, data protection, reporting, model, and End User Computing control requirements across ING Americas. The team works closely with business lines, Finance, Risk, Operations, Technology, data owners, data users, data stewards, and global Data Management teams. Together, we translate global standards and regulatory expectations into pragmatic, sustainable, and locally embedded solutions. You will report hierarchically to the Regional Chief Data Officer / Lead Regional Data Office Americas. Responsibilities: Support end-to-end compliant data delivery by embedding data governance, quality, lineage, protection, reporting, and control requirements into the design and implementation of data solutions. jobs.title: Missile Defense Architecture Analyst (PL)
jobs.jd: We are pleased to announce the opening for a Missile Defense Architecture Analyst, who will join our Architecture Engineering team in Huntsville, Alabama. Qualified candidates will be part of an exceptional team supporting the Missile Defense Agency (MDA) mission to develop and deploy a layered Missile Defense System to defend the United States, its deployed forces, allies, and friends from missile attacks in all phases of flight. Responsibilities: The Missile Defense Architecture Analyst will be providing technical support to the Missile Defense Agency on the MDA Technical, Engineering, Advisory and Management Support. The unique, highly qualified SEA Team is critical to ensuring the MDA can rapidly develop and deploy missile defense capabilities to defeat advanced missile threats by aggressively pursuing advanced concepts and technologies for leap-ahead capability in directed energy, hypersonic missile defense, radiation hardened electronics, space-based sensors, and Israeli defense systems. The SEA Team provides comprehensive Missile Defense System test analyses, future Missile Defense System architecture modeling and design, advanced technology analyses, and specialized engineering support to improve the development, testing, and fielding of technical capabilities that are also cybersecure and tamper-proof. This position will support the office of the MDA Chief Architect and join a team developing and employing Benchmark, a performance modeling tool used for concept exploration and evaluation. This team increases the capability of the Missile Defense Agency to envision and define a future architecture that will enable our nation to stay ahead of adversary’s threat developments to ensure the safety of our nation and its allies globally. Duties include: Maintain awareness of performance assessments of the Missile Defense System at the full system level and among contributing weapon systems and update records on any present or future capability gaps that will drive future development efforts Contribute to architecture planning, requirements definition, and development activities at the enterprise level supporting strategic and regional architectures Develop analysis scripts using MATLAB and/or Python to build new capabilities within the Benchmark M&S environment to support trade study analyses for future concepts Conduct runs of the MDA Benchmark tool to perform predictive analysis about potential future missile defense architecture laydowns against theoretical/conceptual future threat environments Basic Qualifications: This position is open only to US Citizens. You must have 7+ years working on missile defense-related or other complex, large DoD program/project or industry equivalent. You must have a Bachelor’s degree in a STEM field such as engineering, physics, or math. Must possess excellent oral and written communication skills and critical thinking abilities. Must be capable of working independently and within teams to solve complex problems. You must possess or have the ability to obtain an active Secret clearance. Preferred Qualifications: Experience producing analysis tools using Matlab and/or Python or a similar scripting language. Familiarity with one or more elements of the Missile Defense System.

jobs.title: Real Estate Market Intelligence Analyst
jobs.jd:
MISSION

Neko is redefining what prevention means, from treating illness when it arrives, to sustaining health before it's ever at risk. Our mission: make data-driven, preventative care accessible to more people, before symptoms appear. 

In a single, non-invasive visit under an hour, proprietary technology and direct clinical care combine to deliver personalised, actionable insights. It's a team that thinks in 10x, not 10%. Every role here plays a part in building a world where prevention is the norm, and where your work genuinely helps people live longer, healthier lives.




ROLE PURPOSE

Neko is opening clinics at pace: from a handful of US sites today to a 2028 cohort in the dozens and a portfolio in the hundreds by 2030. We are looking for a flexible, quantitative analyst to build the market intelligence behind that growth, using GIS, data, and analytics to decide where we open next, why, and how many clinics a market can support. The work runs from market sizing and member analytics through to site, market, and portfolio performance.

This is a build role. Neko is appointment-based, not footfall-driven, so the standard retail playbook does not transfer, and working out what predicts a successful clinic is the core problem. There is no framework to inherit: you will build the models and processes from scratch, and what you build in year one is what the whole portfolio runs on.

You will report to the Head of US Real Estate and work closely with the Transaction Managers, the Real Estate Associates, and our data analytics and engineering teams, in a small team where you help set the standard.




WHAT YOU'LL DELIVER IN THE FIRST 6-12 MONTHS

 - Market sizing: size the addressable member base by market and trade area, and translate it into how many clinics a market can support and in what order we should enter. This is the first priority of the role.

 - Site selection support: give Real Estate the analysis to justify new markets and infill locations, and to decide clinic sizing and spacing, including overlap and cannibalization as density increases.

 - Member data foundation: work with the internal data analytics and engineering teams to set up the full chain, from data collection to aggregation to analysis. Define our ideal member profile, find where those members live and work, and keep refining it as first-party data accumulates.

 - GIS platform, tool agnostic: use GrowthFactor today and own the catchment definitions, data layers, and scoring logic. Document the logic independently of the tool so it moves with us, and help evaluate and onboard the next platform when the time comes. Make the tool usable by Transaction Managers, not only by you.

 - Scoring and forecasting models: maintain a repeatable, defensible site scoring model and demand forecasts built to be re-run. A reforecast after a slipped opening or a shifted plan should be a scenario switch, not a rebuild.

 - Portfolio, market, and site performance: as clinics open, track and review performance at the portfolio, market, and site level. Compare forecast to actual, separate a bad site from a bad market from a bad launch, surface underperformers early, and document what each opening teaches us. Turn those learnings into updated site selection criteria, scoring weights, and sizing and spacing rules, so every new clinic is chosen with better information than the last.

 - Approval memos and cross-functional support: help produce LOI and Lease Approval Memos by coordinating inputs from Real Estate, Design, Construction, and Legal into a clear, one-page recommendation that leadership can decide from.

 - Process design and redesign: own the evaluation processes the team runs on, and version them. Retire what stops working, rebuild what needs it, and write it down so others can run it without you.

 - AI across the Real Estate team: use Claude and custom agents to eliminate your own manual work, then go further. Identify where AI can save broader team time (market research, data pulls, memo drafting, lease and LOI summaries, pipeline reporting), build reusable prompts, skills, and agents, train teammates to use them, and track the time saved. Be honest about where AI output needs human review.

 - Market packs and benchmarks: produce market entry recommendations, ranked pipeline views, and site-level briefs, backed by per-site cost and occupancy benchmarks by market so deal comparison sits on real data.
   
   


MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

 - 3 to 6 years in real estate market analytics, site selection, location intelligence, data science, or strategy, ideally supporting multi-site physical expansion.

 - Hands-on GIS experience with GrowthFactor, Esri ArcGIS, Kalibrate, Buxton, SiteZeus, Placer, or similar. We care more that you understand catchment and scoring logic than that you know any one tool, because the tool will change.

 - Strong market sizing and quantitative skills: penetration and capture modeling, regression or other predictive approaches, and scenario and sensitivity analysis. Excel to a high standard.

 - Comfort with census, consumer spend, mobility, and first-party data, and honesty about the limits of each.

 - Financial literacy: you can build a basic site pro forma, calculate payback and break-even, and connect a demand forecast to a real estate decision.

 - Flexibility. You can tear down your own model without ego, rebuild it when the facts change, and stay organized while priorities shift.

 - Clear communication and intellectual honesty. You can defend an assumption to a skeptical executive in two minutes, name the two things most likely to be wrong, and say early when the data does not support the answer people want.


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - SQL or Python, which helps you work alongside engineers.

 - Specific, demonstrable use of AI to speed up analytical work, and real interest in teaching others to do the same.

 - Exposure to healthcare or regulated markets, or to European or multi-region expansion.

jobs.title: Analyst - Pricing Optimization
jobs.jd: About the Role The Pricing Optimization Associate supports pricing analytics and decision support across Gap brand. In this role, you will complete foundational analyses and prepare inputs for pricing strategy, price testing, competitive pricing insights, pricing architecture, promotion scenario planning, markdown optimization, yield management, and forecast tuning. This role operates as part of Gap Inc.'s Pricing, Planning Analytics, and Inventory Optimization function, working with business partners and more experienced team members while following consistent decision standards, approved AI-enabled tools, and transparent analytical methods. What You'll Do Analytical Execution Complete recurring pricing analyses, data preparation, model inputs, scenario runs, reporting, and recommendation materials using established methods and templates. Check data and outputs for completeness and accuracy; identify inconsistencies, risks, and patterns, and escalate questions when needed. Prepare clear summaries, visuals, and decision-support materials that explain findings and relevant business implications. Maintain accurate records of assumptions, outputs, approvals, actions, and hindsights in the decision log. Scenario Support and Insight Development Support pricing, promotion, markdown, and yield-management scenarios; learn how revenue, margin, sell-through, customer value, and inventory exposure shape trade-offs. Analyze elasticity, competitive, category, channel, and customer signals and summarize implications for pricing recommendations and guardrails. Coordinate with GMM, Merchandising, Planning, Inventory Optimization, Pricing Operations, and Finance to gather inputs, confirm execution constraints, and support approved price actions. Share analyses with peers across Planning, Pricing, and Inventory Optimization to connect work and reduce siloed execution. Tools, AI and Continuous Learning Use approved AI-enabled tools, models, dashboards, and agents responsibly; validate outputs against source data, business context, and known constraints, seeking guidance for exceptions. Build knowledge of Gap Inc. planning, pricing, inventory, merchandising, and financial processes and apply that knowledge to assigned work. Follow established workflows and contribute practical ideas to improve templates, data quality, recurring work, and the usability of insights. Business Partnership and Quality Contribution Deliver accurate, timely work; communicate progress and risks, seek feedback, and bring curiosity, responsiveness, and a service mindset to business partners and team members. Who You Are Bachelor degree required in business, economics, finance, analytics, mathematics, statistics, engineering, retail, or related field. 1+ years of relevant analytical experience in retail, planning, pricing, inventory, finance, data analytics, consulting, or related fields. Foundational analytical, modeling, communication, and storytelling skills, with the ability to turn data into clear findings and practical next steps. Exposure to retail, apparel, consumer products, consulting, finance, data analytics, planning, pricing, inventory, or merchandising preferred. Comfort using Excel and data tools; exposure to BI platforms, SQL, Python, forecasting, optimization, pricing tools, or AI-enabled workflows preferred. Structured learner who follows established methods, asks thoughtful questions, and communicates clearly. Commercially curious and detail-oriented; interested in how customer, product, revenue, margin, inventory, service, and execution factors connect. Enterprise-minded and brand-aware; applies common standards while learning relevant brand context. Comfortable using AI-enabled tools and agentic workflows with human review, appropriate validation, and timely escalation of exceptions or risks. Collaborative team member who builds trust, responds with urgency, welcomes feedback, and contributes to continuous improvement.

jobs.title: Pricing Strategy Analyst (Remote)
jobs.jd: We're looking for a Pricing Strategy Analyst to join Procore's Corporate Strategy team. In this role, you'll be the data and analytics engine behind our pricing, packaging, and monetization strategy, turning transaction, sales, and product data into the commercial signals that inform our decisions. You'll also lead smaller pricing initiatives across the full Procore portfolio, including our emerging AI offerings. The primary goal of this role is to make sure Procore's pricing decisions are grounded in clear, accurate, and well-sourced data. As a Pricing Strategy Analyst , you'll partner with Product, Sales, Finance, and Marketing to analyze how our pricing and packaging perform in the market and to build the visibility needed to improve them. Use your structured problem-solving, data analysis, and executive communication skills to shape how Procore captures value from what we build and buy. If you want hands-on work to drive top line growth and connect everyone in construction, apply today and join our team! This position reports to the Senior Manager of Pricing & Monetization Strategy and can be based remotely in the US. We're looking for someone to join us immediately. What you'll do: Lead pricing and packaging initiatives from hypothesis through recommendation, in partnership with Product, Sales, Finance, and Marketing Build and stress-test the business case behind pricing decisions, including segment-level performance, cannibalization-adjusted ARR impact, and migration and monetization sizing. Analyze transaction, bookings, discounting, and product data to identify the commercial signals that explain how our pricing and packaging perform, and diagnose the root cause when they underperform, whether it is package design, sales execution, or market fit. Design and run market, competitive, and willingness-to-pay research, including win/loss and price elasticity analysis, to pressure-test pricing hypotheses before they reach leadership. Build and maintain pricing and packaging reporting and dashboards that give Product, Sales, and Finance visibility into performance, working with data teams to keep metrics and data sources accurate and consistent. Translate analysis into a small number of clear, claim-driven recommendations, present them to executive leaders, and defend them under challenge. Partner with Pricing Operations, Sales, Customer Success, Deal Desk, and Marketing to make sure approved decisions are operationalized and communicated to the field. What we’re looking for: Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, Economics, Statistics, or a related field. 3+ years of experience in pricing, monetization, strategy, business or data analytics, financial planning and analysis, or consulting wi th 2+ y ears inside a pricing or monetization practice at a top-tier strategy firm Track record of framing ambiguous problems into clear analytical frameworks and presenting recommendations to cross-functional and senior audiences. Experience leading projects or workstreams from analysis through recommendation, with the ability to balance multiple priorities. Advanced Excel and financial modeling skills, with experience building revenue impact and unit economics models. Hands-on experience querying and analyzing large datasets (e.g., SQL), building reports in a BI tool (e.g., Tableau, Power BI) is a plus Ability to synthesize qualitative inputs, such as call transcripts and field feedback, into clear themes that support pricing recommendations. Cross-functional collaboration and influence skills, with experience partnering with Product, Sales, Finance, and Marketing teams. Familiarity with B2B SaaS metrics (e.g., ARR, net revenue retention, win rate, discount rate) is a plus Curiosity, high agency, and an owner’s mindset with a strong bias for action. Additional Information Base Pay Range: 81,600.00 - 112,200.00 USD Annual This role may also be eligible for Equity Compensation and/or Bonus Incentive Compensation. Procore is committed to offering competitive, fair, and commensurate compensation. Actual compensation will be based on a candidate’s job-related skills, experience, education or training, and location. For Los Angeles County (unincorporated) Candidates: Procore will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records, in accordance with the requirements of applicable federal, state, and local laws, including the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act. A criminal history may have a direct, adverse, and negative relationship on the following job duties, potentially resulting in the withdrawal of the conditional offer of employment: 1. appropriately managing, accessing, and handling confidential information including proprietary and trade secret information, as well as accessing Procore's information technology systems and platforms; 2. interacting with and occasionally having unsupervised contact with internal/external customers, stakeholders, and/or colleagues; and 3. exercising sound judgment.

jobs.title: Data Center Infrastructure Architect
jobs.jd:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Industrial Compute team is building and productizing infrastructure capabilities that help organizations deploy and operate advanced AI systems at scale. The team works across AI hardware, systems engineering, physical infrastructure, and customer delivery to turn emerging technologies into reliable, repeatable infrastructure solutions.

Our work sits at the intersection of technical strategy, product development, engineering, and deployment. We partner closely with customers and internal engineering teams to solve complex infrastructure challenges spanning compute, power, cooling, controls, and facility efficiency.

About the Role

We are seeking a senior, hands-on Data Center Infrastructure Architect to develop and optimize the physical infrastructure required for large-scale AI deployments.

This is a broad technical role spanning data center architecture, electrical and mechanical systems, high-density compute, controls, telemetry, and digital modeling. You will use simulation, operational data, and digital-twin approaches to evaluate infrastructure designs, identify system-level constraints, and improve efficiency, reliability, cost, and speed of deployment.

The ideal candidate can move fluidly between first-principles analysis, facility and equipment design, computational modeling, engineering review, and real-world implementation. You should be comfortable working across disciplines rather than operating solely within electrical, mechanical, or software boundaries.

Key Responsibilities

 - Define system-level architectures for high-density AI data centers across power, cooling, IT equipment, controls, and facility infrastructure.

 - Develop digital twins and other computational models that represent the behavior of data center systems under changing workloads, environmental conditions, equipment configurations, and failure scenarios.

 - Use design and operational data to identify constraints, improve PUE and related efficiency metrics, and optimize capacity, reliability, water consumption, cost, and deployment schedules.

 - Evaluate tradeoffs across electrical topology, cooling architecture, rack density, redundancy, controls, maintainability, constructability, and operational complexity.

 - Translate evolving AI hardware requirements into practical facility, rack, power, and thermal architectures.

 - Establish reference architectures, modeling standards, design assumptions, performance requirements, and validation methodologies that can be reused across customer deployments.

 - Partner with software, data, controls, hardware, mechanical, electrical, construction, commissioning, and operations teams to connect digital models with real infrastructure behavior.

 - Integrate telemetry from systems such as BMS, EPMS, DCIM, SCADA, equipment controllers, and IT hardware into modeling and optimization workflows.

 - Lead technical reviews of customer and partner designs, identify material risks, and recommend changes grounded in quantitative analysis.

 - Work with customers and delivery teams to adapt reference solutions to site-specific constraints while preserving performance, reliability, and efficiency objectives.

 - Support pilots, commissioning, performance testing, and post-deployment analysis to validate models and continuously improve infrastructure designs.

 - Help shape the technical roadmap for Industrial Compute’s physical-infrastructure products and engineering services.

Qualifications

 - Significant experience designing or optimizing hyperscale data centers, large mission-critical facilities, or comparable infrastructure systems.

 - Broad knowledge of data center electrical and mechanical systems, including power distribution, backup power, thermal management, liquid cooling, heat rejection, controls, and monitoring.

 - Experience making system-level design decisions across multiple engineering disciplines.

 - Experience developing or applying simulation, optimization, digital-twin, or physics-based modeling techniques to physical infrastructure.

 - Strong understanding of data center efficiency and performance metrics, including PUE, WUE, utilization, capacity, reliability, and total cost of ownership.

 - Experience working with operational telemetry and translating real-world system behavior into design improvements.

 - Ability to evaluate complex tradeoffs involving performance, reliability, cost, schedule, scalability, sustainability, and maintainability.

 - Demonstrated ability to lead technical work in ambiguous, rapidly changing environments.

 - Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex engineering decisions to customers, executives, and cross-functional teams.

 - Bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, systems engineering, applied physics, or a related technical discipline.

Preferred Skills

 - Experience with high-density GPU clusters and direct-to-chip liquid cooling.

 - Experience connecting facility models with workload, rack, server, or chip-level power and thermal behavior.

 - Familiarity with modeling or engineering tools such as Modelica, MATLAB/Simulink, Python, EnergyPlus, computational fluid dynamics tools, or equivalent platforms.

 - Experience with BMS, EPMS, DCIM, SCADA, PLCs, data historians, or industrial controls.

 - Experience developing reference designs or new infrastructure architectures within a hyperscaler, data center operator, advanced engineering organization, or major design consultancy.

 - Experience taking an infrastructure concept from modeling and prototype validation through deployment and operational feedback.

 - Advanced degree in an engineering or scientific discipline.

Success in the First Year

 - Establish a credible system-level model of power, cooling, compute, and facility behavior for priority Industrial Compute use cases.

 - Identify and validate meaningful opportunities to improve efficiency, capacity, reliability, or deployment cost.

 - Deliver reusable reference architectures and engineering methodologies for customer deployments.

 - Create a repeatable feedback loop connecting modeling, operational telemetry, commissioning results, and future design decisions.

 - Become a trusted technical partner to internal engineering teams, customers, and infrastructure delivery partners.



About OpenAI

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. 

We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic.

jobs.jd:
COMPANY OVERVIEW

Deepgram is the leading platform underpinning the emerging trillion-dollar Voice AI economy, providing real-time APIs for speech-to-text (STT), text-to-speech (TTS), and building production-grade voice agents at scale. More than 200,000 developers and 1,300+ organizations build voice offerings that are ‘Powered by Deepgram’, including Twilio, Cloudflare, Sierra, Decagon, Vapi, Daily, Cresta, Granola, and Jack in the Box. Deepgram’s voice-native foundation models are accessed through cloud APIs or as self-hosted and on-premises software, with unmatched accuracy, low latency, and cost efficiency. Backed by a recent Series C led by leading global investors and strategic partners, Deepgram has processed over 50,000 years of audio and transcribed more than 1 trillion words. There is no organization in the world that understands voice better than Deepgram.




COMPANY OPERATING RHYTHM

At Deepgram, we expect an AI-first mindset—AI use and comfort aren’t optional, they’re core to how we operate, innovate, and measure performance.

Every team member who works at Deepgram is expected to actively use and experiment with advanced AI tools, and even build your own into your everyday work. We measure how effectively AI is applied to deliver results, and consistent, creative use of the latest AI capabilities is key to success here. Candidates should be comfortable adopting new models and modes quickly, integrating AI into their workflows, and continuously pushing the boundaries of what these technologies can do.

Additionally, we move at the pace of AI. Change is rapid, and you can expect your day-to-day work to evolve just as quickly. This may not be the right role if you’re not excited to experiment, adapt, think on your feet, and learn constantly, or if you’re seeking something highly prescriptive with a traditional 9-to-5.




TEAM OVERVIEW

Marketing Operations keeps Deepgram's go-to-market engine measurable. As our first Marketing & GTM Data Analyst, you'll build the reporting and analytics function rather than inherit a finished one, and own the answer to what's working and where to invest next. You'll partner with the Director of Marketing Operations on the weekly GTM report leadership reads, and with our Decision Intelligence and Data Engineering teams on AI analytics agents and the GTM data foundation. Your work will power Marketing, Product, SDR, AE, Partnerships, and RevOps.




KEY GOALS

 - Automate recurring GTM analytics with Decision Intelligence, designing and improving AI agents for weekly reporting, campaign and sales play readouts, scoring-model checks, and anomaly alerts, as the GTM expert who writes evaluation cases and QAs their output.

 - Own Marketing and GTM KPI definitions, calculation logic, and the weekly report leadership reads, with a clear narrative on what changed and why.

 - Measure marketing campaigns and SDR/AE sales plays from first touch through closed-won, using pre/post and cohort analysis to say what to scale, fix, or stop.

 - Create reusable campaign and sales play reporting templates with consistent definitions, time windows, and attribution rules, structured so AI agents can generate first drafts.

 - Own Dreamdata and evolve our attribution practices (multi-touch, sourcing rules, SDR credit, partner attribution), reconcile them with Salesforce and HubSpot, and turn attribution into budget recommendations.

 - Evaluate and improve MQL, PQL, and account intent scoring models, with automated monitoring of precision, coverage, and conversion lift by score.

 - Define and report partner and business development performance, including partner-sourced and influenced pipeline, co-marketing results, and performance by tier.

 - Define GTM source-of-truth datasets with Data Engineering and Decision Intelligence, write the semantic context AI analytics agents rely on, and drive data quality fixes upstream.


MINIMUM SKILLS, KNOWLEDGE & CAPABILITIES

 - Turns vague or complex requests ("did re:Invent work?", "why is pipeline soft?") into clear, answerable questions before touching data, and pushes back constructively when the question is wrong.

 - Understands the B2B funnel (MQL, SAL, SQL, Closed Won) and how marketing, product-led, partner, SDR, and AE motions interact, and explains why the numbers look the way they do.

 - Writes strong SQL directly in a warehouse and across Salesforce objects (Leads, Contacts, Campaigns, Campaign Members, Opportunities, custom objects).

 - Reconciles messy data across systems, holds a high bar for what counts as right, and fixes problems at the source rather than patching downstream.

 - Has owned or improved a multi-touch attribution setup and reconciled it with CRM data.

 - Evaluates or tunes lead, PQL, or account scoring models and measures whether they improve conversion.

 - Operates AI-native: builds AI agents or agentic workflows for analytics (e.g., Claude Code, MCP servers, n8n), automates recurring analysis, and writes the evaluation cases and context agents need to be accurate.

 - Builds dashboards and recurring reports in a BI tool that people rely on and act on, with a narrative sized for leadership.

 - Owns KPI definitions so the same number means the same thing everywhere.


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS (NICE-TO-HAVE, NOT REQUIRED)

 - Typically ~3–5 years in marketing analytics, GTM or revenue analytics, or a similar analytical role at a B2B SaaS company, or equivalent demonstrated experience.

 - Hands-on with Dreamdata, HockeyStack, Bizible, or a similar attribution tool, plus HubSpot and Salesforce reporting.

 - Python, and experience with dbt, semantic layers, or metric stores.

 - Worked with intent data or partner attribution.

 - Experience at a usage-based, developer-focused, or product-led business.


OUR VALUES

 - Be You — bring your whole self and a different perspective; diverse viewpoints make our products better.

 - Be Curious — challenge the status quo, keep learning, and ask 'how might we?' instead of accepting limits.

 - Grow Together — push each other to do great work, treat feedback as a gift, and leave the drama out.

 - Do the Right Thing — act with integrity and candor, assume best intent, choose ethics over expediency.

 - Think Smart. Act Fast. — weigh the high-leverage options, decide, and move; no analysis paralysis.

 - Put the Customer First — listen with empathy, understand their goals, and let their success drive ours.



We know the confidence gap and imposter syndrome can get in the way of meeting great candidates — so please don't hesitate to apply. We'd love to hear from you.

Notice: We're aware of individuals impersonating Deepgram recruiters. All legitimate Deepgram recruiting communication comes from an @deepgram.com http://deepgram.com email address. If you've received a message claiming to be Deepgram, please forward it to careers@deepgram.com.

jobs.jd: Convene Hospitality Group (CHG) operates a global portfolio of lifestyle brands focused on creating places and experiences that bring people together. The company designs, develops, and operates hospitality-driven destinations to host gatherings of all kinds, ranging from small corporate meetings to immersive brand activations and beyond. We love bringing people together in person, and that passion for great experiences extends to our employees as well. If you're interested in creating inspiring moments of connection, consider joining our team. Analytics Engineer We’re hiring Analytics Engineers to join Convene Hospitality Group’s (CHG) Technology organization. We’re building out the foundational platform to democratize data at CHG so that a venue GM, a finance lead, and an AI agent are all able to ask a question and get the same trusted answer. Analytics engineers own the full path from ingestion to visualization, including governance and observability. You’ll bring data in from source systems, model it through bronze, silver, and gold, define the semantic layer, and breathe life into the visualizations, conversational analytics, and business agents that teams rely on to make decisions. You’ll join the Data Platform team, reporting to its Engineering Manager, and work closely with other analytics engineers and business partners across the company. You’ll build on Snowflake, dbt, and Fivetran, using Snowflake-native capabilities like semantic views and Cortex to power ThoughtSpot and beyond. What You’ll Do: Partner with the business. Work with Finance, Sales, Operations, and venue teams to understand their needs and turn them into models and metrics they trust. Own ingestion for your domains. Set up and maintain Fivetran connectors, land data in bronze, and handle schema drift and load failures. Model the business. Build dbt models that move data through bronze, silver, and gold, and shape gold around how CHG runs so people outside the data team can understand and use it. Own the semantic layer. Set metrics, dimensions, and relationships so a number means the same thing in a dashboard, a search, or an agent’s answer. Tune synonyms and descriptions so a model picks the right measure, trace wrong answers to the root cause, and help us decide where each definition lives. Power self-service in ThoughtSpot. Build the models and Liveboards that let teams explore data on their own, and turn the questions people actually ask into new test cases. Own the quality of conversational analytics. Test answers the way you’d test code. Build and maintain a golden question set of real business questions paired with certified answers as your test cases, run them as a regression suite on every model or semantic change, and block releases that fail. Back your models with dbt tests and clear documentation. Apply governance day to day. Tag sensitive data at ingestion, apply access controls such as tag-based masking and row access policies, and follow the standards the team sets, so an agent only returns what the person asking is allowed to see. Keep it fast and fresh. Monitor freshness, data quality, and pipeline health so problems surface to you before they reach a dashboard or an agent’s answer. Tune query and model performance, from incremental dbt models to warehouse sizing, so answers come back fast and Snowflake costs stay in check. Work AI-native. Lead with specs, then hand agents end-to-end tasks, from exploring source data to building models, tests, and documentation. Let agents run loose in the wild (with some guardrails in place). You hold agent and human work to the same review bar, so code from Claude and code from a teammate get the same scrutiny. Share what you learn, and help set the playbook for agentic data work. What We Look For: You have 3+ years in analytics engineering, data engineering, or BI development, building data products people rely on. You write strong SQL and have built and maintained dbt models in production. You’ve worked in a cloud data warehouse, ideally Snowflake. You’ve worked with ELT ingestion tools like Fivetran and can troubleshoot source-data issues such as schema changes, late-arriving data, and API limits. You understand data modeling: dimensional models, medallion layering, and clear reasoning about grain, slowly changing dimensions, and event lifecycles. You’ve built dashboards or self-service data products that people use to make decisions. You test and document your work as a habit. You’re curious about the business. You ask what decision a request supports before you start building. You use AI agents for real multi-step work, like writing SQL and dbt models, generating tests, and drafting documentation, and you verify what they produce. You explain your work clearly to technical and non-technical partners. You take ownership. You see work through, ask for help when you’re stuck, and look for ways to make things better. Bonus Points You’ve evaluated LLM or natural-language analytics output, for example with golden sets or regression testing. You’ve worked in hospitality, events, real estate, or another customer-centric, multi-location business. jobs.title: Data Scientist Fellow — AI/ML
jobs.jd: (ID: 2026-3885) Axle is a bioscience and information technology company that offers advancements in translational research, biomedical informatics, and data science applications to research centers and healthcare organizations nationally and abroad. With experts in biomedical science, software engineering, and program management, we focus on developing and applying research tools and techniques to empower decision-making and accelerate research discoveries. We work with some of the top research organizations and facilities in the country including multiple institutes at the National Institutes of Health (NIH). Benefits We Offer: 100% Medical, Dental & Vision Coverage for Employees Paid Time Off and Paid Holidays 401K match up to 5% Educational Benefits for Career Growth Employee Referral Bonus Flexible Spending Accounts: Healthcare (FSA) Parking Reimbursement Account (PRK) Dependent Care Assistant Program (DCAP) Transportation Reimbursement Account (TRN) Position Overview The Data Scientist Fellow will develop computational models to predict and optimize organoid growth and differentiation protocols in support of the SOM Center. The incumbent will apply advanced machine learning techniques to organoid standardization and contribute to the development of predictive models for tissue engineering applications. Key Responsibilities Model development. Design and implement machine learning models that predict organoid development outcomes based on protocol parameters, environmental conditions, and molecular characterization data. In silico simulation. Develop in silico models that correspond to organoid growth, maturation, and characterize phenotype while identifying optimal conditions for reproducible organoid generation. Feedback systems. Establish feedback loops between experimental validation and computational prediction in order to iteratively refine and understand protocol standardization. Interdisciplinary collaboration. Work with experimental teams to design characterization and validation experiments and with bioinformatics scientists to integrate multi-modal datasets. Required Qualifications Education. Doctoral degree (PhD) in computer science, engineering, applied mathematics, or a related field, with demonstrated experience in AI/ML model development. jobs.jd: About General Atlantic General Atlantic is a leading global investor with more than four and a half decades of experience providing capital and strategic support for over 885 companies throughout its history. Established in 1980, General Atlantic continues to be a dedicated partner to visionary founders and investors seeking to build dynamic businesses and create lasting value. Guided by the conviction that entrepreneurs can be incredible agents of transformational change, the firm combines a collaborative global approach, sector specific expertise, a long-term investment horizon, and a deep understanding of growth drivers to partner with and scale innovative businesses around the world. The firm leverages its patient capital, operational expertise, and global platform to support a diversified investment platform spanning Growth Equity, Infrastructure, and Strategic Solutions. General Atlantic manages approximately $126 billion in assets under management, inclusive of all strategies, as of March 31, 2026, with more than 900 professionals in 20 countries across five regions. For more information on General Atlantic, please visit www.generalatlantic.com. Position Summary General Atlantic is looking to hire an Analyst to support the Portfolio Management team. This role is a two-year program (with the ability to extend, depending on performance and business need). The Portfolio Management team provides a senior-level analytics and risk management function at the firm, working closely with our senior leaders and investment team members, and partnering with our fundraising, finance operations, valuations, and capital markets teams. The Portfolio Management team leverages portfolio company data to identify risks and opportunities and assess the general health of our portfolio for the senior-level Portfolio Committee. The team also leverages this data for internal and external reporting, including directly with investors. This generalist role offers a broad view of GA’s 200+ portfolio companies and of the firm itself. The Analyst will partner with professionals across the firm while serving a vital role to the efficiency and effectiveness of the Portfolio Management team. Responsibilities Support the quarterly financial planning cycles across portfolio companies, consolidating information and providing analyses to leadership via Portfolio Committee meetings. Collaborate across the firm working with Investment, Capital Solutions, Marketing, Legal, Accounting, and Finance professionals. Collect, review, and analyze portfolio company-level data across GA’s 250+ portfolio companies. Analyze investment performance, returns, and key metrics to draw insights and conclusions at both the company and fund/portfolio levels. Leverage portfolio data to develop metrics, solve problems, and prepare materials for senior-level audiences influencing decision-making. Synthesize findings across the portfolio and macro data to deliver thoughtful analysis and actionable insights. Support the design and implementation of process improvement and new technology initiatives to drive scalable analysis and insight across the team and firm. Use AI tools in day-to-day work to automate analysis and reporting, and to speed up research and data synthesis. Identify and pilot new ways to apply AI to portfolio data and team workflows, and share what works with colleagues. Qualifications Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, or a related field preferred; equivalent work experience considered. At least 1 year of experience in the consulting, accounting, corporate finance, or banking industry. Strong understanding of financial statements – P&L, Balance Sheet, and Cash Flow (i.e., ability to interpret financial data and related management information). Ability to develop presentations leveraging creativity, thoughtful business judgment and problem solving. Experience working with multiple stakeholders, effective verbal and written communication skills, and ability to synthesize information. Excellent Microsoft Office skills, including Excel and PowerPoint. Self-motivated, with a demonstrated ability to own specific parts of projects and work independently with minimal supervision. Intellectually curious, resourceful, and team-oriented, with a collaborative approach to problem solving. jobs.title: Business Systems Analyst, Scientific Systems
jobs.jd: Imagine if you had the skills, knowledge, and teammates to both understand the root of the world’s most pressing problems and build the technologies and companies best positioned to solve them. RA Capital has done exactly that for more than two decades, backing bold ideas in medicines to further human health and now expanding into Planetary Health to improve how efficiently we utilize the world’s precious resources. RA Capital is among the leading providers of capital and services to the most promising innovators in the world. We invest flexibly—seed to IPO and beyond, anywhere in the world—with $10 B+ under management and a culture that prizes curiosity, rigor, and collaborative debate. We are investors who not only fund companies but get elbow deep in building them. From helping them recruit talent to helping them recruit patients for their studies to helping match them to strategic partners and even going to Washington to win reforms, RA Capital’s large team has people with nearly every relevant expertise one might need to turn an idea into a cure that actually helps people. If you live for first-principles problem-solving with great colleagues, thrive on complexity, and want to do meaningful work that ripples across industries and ecosystems, you’ll feel at home at RA Capital. Here, questions are welcomed, ideas are tested, and victories are shared. Even our lawyers are creative and engaging. And don’t get us started on our compliance team’s wicked sense of humor; nothing about what we do is boring. Are you ready to bring your creativity, discipline and collaborative spirit to help us invent the future? Join us and you’ll collaborate daily with investors, founders, physicians, biologists, engineers, economists, and reform advocates who think in systems and act with urgency. Join us to invent a happier, healthier, more productive future - and have fun doing it. Role Overview RA Capital is seeking a Business Systems Analyst, Scientific & Venture Systems to support our Raven and Venture teams. Reporting to the Technology Business Partner, Raven and Venture, you will work with scientists, company builders, and business stakeholders to translate research and operational workflows into practical technology solutions. This hands-on role combines business analysis, scientific platform administration, and software implementation. You will configure and administer scientific systems, develop programmatic integrations, and automate workflows, owning solutions from discovery through deployment and ongoing support. Use AI-assisted development tools to accelerate delivery while independently reviewing, testing, and validating generated code and recommendations. Support vendor evaluation and implementation, coordinate technical partners, and troubleshoot issues across the systems you configure and support. Plan and conduct system and user acceptance testing, maintain documentation and user guides, and train users through rollout and adoption. Manage smaller projects and workstreams, communicating scope, milestones, dependencies, and risks while identifying opportunities for ongoing improvement. Key Requirements Bachelor’s degree in biology, chemistry, bioengineering, computer science, or a related scientific or technical field. 2–5 years of experience in solutions engineering, scientific software implementation, business systems analysis, or a related role, ideally with a life sciences software provider or within a biotech organization. Practical programming experience, including the ability to independently read, write, debug, test, and validate code and work with REST APIs. Foundational SQL skills, including joins, parameterized queries, and data validation. Ability to evaluate and troubleshoot AI-generated code using independent programming knowledge and judgment. Experience working directly with scientific/clinical users or customers to learn research workflows quickly and translate their needs into technical solutions. Strong requirements-gathering, process mapping, and documentation skills, with close attention to detail. Clear communication with technical and non-technical colleagues, sound judgment, and a willingness to raise questions and collaborate when requirements or solutions are uncertain. Ability to work on a hybrid schedule in our Boston office. Must be authorized to work in the United States without sponsorship now or in the future. We cannot provide visa sponsorship, visa transfers, or sponsorship for practical training programs. Experience implementing software across multiple customers, research teams, or organizations. Experience configuring Notion workspaces, teamspaces, templates, integrations, and automations. Experience with AI-assisted development tools such as Claude Code or Codex, or integration and automation platforms. Working knowledge of data platforms or cloud environments such as Databricks, Snowflake, AWS or GCP. jobs.title: Commodity Supply Analyst I
jobs.jd: Are you an innovative and adaptable self-starter who enjoys working on a high energy and technical team to perform data analysis and problem solving? Then the Commodity Supply Analyst 1 position may be the job for you! Commodity Supply Analyst provide leadership and support to our Supply & Risk Management, Accounting, Finance & Treasury, Operations, and Sales divisions by preparing, analyzing, and reporting complex data for both internal and external customers. Our Commodity Supply Analyst are responsible for ensuring that all financial, regulatory, and contractual obligations are met. Are you a fit? This role will uncover insights and trends for actionable storytelling opportunities, guide marketing strategy, and inform cross-functional partners on social, cultural, and influencer trends. Reporting to the Sr. Manager, Analytics & Strategy, this position is ideal for someone who thrives in building scalable analytics systems while staying deeply connected to cultural and platform trends and developments. We're looking for a data-minded storyteller who lives at the intersection of social media and analytics. You'll own reporting and measurement for earned conversation tied to tours, on-sales, and artist activations. This is a great fit for someone who's equally comfortable in a spreadsheet and a comment section. WHAT THIS ROLE WILL DO Own measurement and analysis of earned social conversation: mentions, share of voice, sentiment, engagement on non-owned posts, organic reach, and virality across Instagram, TikTok, X, YouTube, and emerging platforms. Run social listening across tour cycles (from announcements, on-sales to live moments), tracking fan sentiment, conversation volume, and flagging shifts in real time. Measure fan- and creator-generated content (UGC): what's made, how it spreads, which moments drive organic amplification, and how artists, media, and fan accounts pick it up. Build and maintain dashboards and recurring reports (daily, weekly, campaign-level, ad-hoc, and post-mortem), using Boolean logic to sharpen queries and insights delivery. Run competitive and benchmark analysis to contextualize our performance. Build alert systems for emerging artist topics, trends, and brand risks, supporting Community Management, Marketing, and PR/Comms in shaping response messaging. Partner with social listening-tool vendors and cross-functional teams to improve benchmarks, KPIs, alerts, and depth of insight. Uncover fan insights through audience demographics to help guide campaign planning WHAT THIS PERSON WILL BRING 2–4 years in social media analytics, social listening, and/or digital insights with a focus on earned measurement (agency or in-house social team preferred). Hands-on experience with social listening and publishing tools (Meltwater, Brandwatch, Sprout, Quid, etc.) plus platform-native analytics. Comfortable with audience demographic tools such as Audiense as well as platform follower demographics through CreatorIQ. Fluency in earned-social metrics (share of voice, sentiment, mention volume) and a clear sense of which ones actually matter. Strong Excel/Google Sheets skills and a solid grasp of Boolean logic for query development. Proven ability to own analytics end-to-end (query design, reporting, dashboard development and maintenance), with a track record of spotting and fixing gaps in reporting infrastructure. Deep understanding of social platforms as both a fan and an analyst: how conversation forms, why things spread, what fans respond to, plus genuine curiosity about cultural trends, emerging formats, and creator marketing. Strong communication skills: you can turn a spike in conversation into a one-slide "so what" for non-technical stakeholders. Detail-oriented, organized, and able to juggle multiple projects and deadlines under pressure. A proactive, collaborative team player who flags insights before they're asked for and adapts to evolving leadership needs. Bachelor's degree in Marketing, Analytics, or a related field. NICE TO HAVE: Passion for live music, touring, and artist marketing. Experience with sentiment analysis, text/topic classification, or unstructured conversation data. Familiarity with creator/influencer earned-coverage measurement. Experience connecting earned social signals to broader marketing or fan-growth outcomes. jobs.title: Amazon Operations Analyst
jobs.jd: Trove Brands is a privately-held house of brands including BlenderBottle®, Owala®, Whiskware®, and Eco-Brite®. Our patented and best-selling products are designed to simplify and improve everyday life with leading-edge innovation, incomparable quality, and aspirational style. A career at Trove Brands is not about punching the clock. It’s about embracing exciting and fast-paced opportunities that sharpen your skills, drive innovation, and play an integral role in growing our global reach. Your work will not only impact the company, it will impact the lives of millions of people around the world. When you step up to a career at Trove, you step up to cutting-edge excellence. You sign up for bold action and invigorating synergy. You agree to face—and break through—new challenges every single day. The Amazon Operations Analyst supports the growth and operational performance of Trove Brands' Amazon US 1P business through data analysis, business intelligence, inventory visibility, and operational execution. This role is responsible for analyzing sales performance, identifying lost sales opportunities, monitoring inventory trends, tracking purchase orders, and providing actionable business insights. Working closely with Amazon Sales, Sales Forecasting, Supply Chain, Logistics, Finance, and other cross-functional teams, this role helps improve product availability, operational efficiency, and business performance. The ideal candidate is analytical, detail-oriented, and proactive, with the ability to translate complex data into actionable insights that support business growth. Key Responsibilities: Analyze Amazon sales, traffic, conversion, inventory, and operational performance to identify trends, risks, and growth opportunities. Identify lost sales opportunities related to out-of-stocks, inventory gaps, product availability, and purchase order execution. Monitor inventory levels, Amazon demand signals, replenishment trends, and product availability to minimize stockouts. Track Amazon purchase orders from creation through fulfillment and delivery, identifying and resolving operational issues. Monitor key operational KPIs, including PO confirmation rates, fill rates, inventory availability, and fulfillment performance. Develop and maintain dashboards and reporting to provide visibility into sales performance, inventory health, and business opportunities. Analyze ASIN performance, sell-through, and category trends to identify underperformance and competitive opportunities. Support new product launches and promotional events by monitoring inventory readiness, purchase orders, and operational risks. Collaborate with Amazon Sales, Sales Forecasting, Supply Chain, Logistics, EDI/Processing, and Finance to improve operational execution. Monitor Amazon Vendor Central operations and help ensure accurate product, order, and inventory information. Leverage AI tools, automation, and data visualization to streamline reporting, improve processes, and deliver actionable insights. Required Qualifications: 1-3 years of experience in eCommerce, retail analytics, sales operations, supply chain, marketplace operations, or a related field. Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret large datasets and translate findings into actionable insights. Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, including PivotTables, lookups, and data analysis. Experience working with data analysis, reporting, or visualization tools. Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and ability to manage multiple priorities. Ability to identify operational challenges, troubleshoot issues, and recommend effective solutions. Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to collaborate across departments. Ability to learn new systems, processes, and reporting platforms quickly. Experience in retail or consumer packaged goods (CPG) environments. Background in retail analytics, sales planning, or supply chain operations supporting major retailers. jobs.title: Collections Analyst
jobs.jd: This is Adyen Adyen provides payments, data, and financial products in a single solution for customers like Meta, Uber, H&M, and Microsoft - making us the financial technology platform of choice. At Adyen, everything we do is engineered for ambition. For our teams, we create an environment with opportunities for our people to succeed, backed by the culture and support to ensure they are enabled to truly own their careers. We are motivated individuals who tackle unique technical challenges at scale and solve them as a team. Together, we deliver innovative and ethical solutions that help businesses achieve their ambitions faster. About the team Credit Risk Operations owns Adyen's global arrears and collections flow for our financial products. When a merchant falls behind on repayment, we work to recover what is owed while keeping the relationship intact and staying fully compliant. We sit at the intersection of Credit Risk, Product, Finance, Legal and our second-line Risk and Compliance teams. The team is growing quickly, so the processes, tooling and playbooks you help build now will shape how Adyen collects at scale. What you'll do As a Collections Analyst in Chicago, you will own a portfolio of US merchants in arrears across Adyen's financial products: cash advances, capital loans, charge cards, overdrafts and hardware financing. You will resolve each case end to end, from first outreach to repayment plan, recovery or escalation. Alongside your caseload, you will help turn a fast-growing operation into a scalable, compliant and increasingly automated one. You will run your own portfolio independently, within agreed playbooks and approval limits. You will escalate exceptions such as settlements, write-offs and legal action to senior colleagues, and take on more complex accounts as you grow.
